simple.meaning: נָגַח (nâgach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to butt with the horns; figuratively, to war against.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 11 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, and 2 more, beginning at Exodus 21:28. Its contexts include birth, family line, firstborn.

occurrences.englishText: “If a bull gores a man or a woman to death, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its meat shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall not be held responsible.
Whether it has gored a son or has gored a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.

If the bull gores a male servant or a female servant, thirty shekels* A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 30 shekels is about 300 grams or about 10.6 ounces. of silver shall be given to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.
Majesty belongs to the firstborn of his herd.
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made himself horns of iron, and said, “Yahweh says, ‘With these you will push the Syrians, until they are consumed.’ ”

For I will not trust in my bow,
Because you thrust with side and with shoulder, and push all the diseased with your horns, until you have scattered them abroad;

I saw the ram pushing westward, northward, and southward. No animals could stand before him. There wasn’t any who could deliver out of his hand; but he did according to his will, and magnified himself.

“At the time of the end the king of the south will contend with him; and the king of the north will come against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, with horsemen, and with many ships. He will enter into the countries, and will overflow and pass through.
